original_question: If Q = {q1, q2, ...} is an infinite set of primes satisfying lim inf_{x -> infinity} (log x / x) |{qi : qi <= x, qi in Q}| > 1/2, does every sufficiently large odd integer 2n + 1 admit a representation qi + qj + qk = 2n + 1 with qi, qj, qk in Q?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, with Proposition 1.2 giving the equivalent density formulation and Theorem 1.3 answering it.
correct_elements: The draft identifies the correct mathematical object (a subset Q of the primes), the correct density threshold (strictly greater than 1/2), the correct additive pattern (representation of odd integers as a sum of three primes from Q), and the correct asymptotic scope ('every sufficiently large odd integer'). It is already very close to the paper's main prime-set question.
missing_details: The ambient set should be stated explicitly as Q \subseteq \mathbb{P}, where \mathbb{P} denotes the set of all prime numbers.
The density hypothesis should be written cleanly in terms of |Q \cap [1,x]|, rather than via an indexed list {q_i}.

Proposition 1.2 supplies the equivalent formulation in terms of lower relative density inside the primes, namely \liminf_{x\to\infty} |Q\cap[1,x]|/\pi(x) > 1/2, where \pi(x) is the prime-counting function.
The odd variable should be quantified as an arbitrary sufficiently large odd integer N, rather than parametrized as 2n+1.
The phrase 'for all sufficiently large odd integers' should be made explicit as: there exists N_0 = N_0(Q) such that every odd integer N \ge N_0 has the required representation.

To make the question fully stand-alone, it should specify whether repetitions are allowed in the representation; in the Goldbach/Vinogradov formulation used here, the three primes are not required to be distinct.
The question should avoid unnecessary enumeration notation Q = {q_1,q_2,\dots} unless an ordering is actually used.
refined_question:
Let Q \subseteq \mathbb{P} be a set of prime numbers such that
\[\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{|Q\cap[1,x]|}{\pi(x)} > \frac12,\]
where \pi(x) denotes the number of primes \le x (equivalently, by Proposition 1.2, \(\liminf_{x\to\infty} (\log x/x)\,|Q\cap[1,x]| > 1/2\)). Must there exist a constant N_0 = N_0(Q) such that every odd integer N \ge N_0 can be written as
\[N=q_1+q_2+q_3\]
with q_1,q_2,q_3 \in Q (not necessarily distinct)?
equivalent_formulation:
Let Q \subseteq \mathbb{P} satisfy
\[\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{\log x}{x}\,|Q\cap[1,x]| > \frac12.\]
Is it true that every sufficiently large odd integer is a sum of three primes from Q?
justification: Your draft is targeting the paper's prime-set problem, namely Conjecture 1.1. The paper then sharpens the hypothesis via Proposition 1.2 by converting Sárközy's original liminf condition into the equivalent lower relative density condition inside the primes. Theorem 1.3 is the corresponding theorem attached to that conjectural formulation. So the paper-faithful stand-alone version should use Q \subseteq \mathbb{P}, an odd integer variable N, an explicit 'there exists N_0(Q)' quantifier, and the equivalent lower-density-in-primes formulation when desired.
